strands.label: The medieval half
strands.note: Offices and dates from 1318 to 1598 that no document has been checked for here. Read as the family's own account of itself until a Zadar notarial fond is opened.

strands.label: Perinuša is not named for Perini
strands.note: This archive once read the by-name Perini as the origin of the place name. It is not: Perinuša is named for the Perinović of Zadar, whom the Franceschi brought in as estate managers. The correction stands on the page.

spines.name: Out of Crete, as refugees
spines.sub: Four generations · Candia to Seget · 1669 to 1790
spines.lede: This archive has said for a year that Crete is «a route, not a tree». Setting the material on one channel shows that it is both — and that the join everyone treated as missing is carried by a Venetian pension office.

strands.label: Giorgio's two sons, named in the deed
strands.note: The 1720 purchase of Catarina Bernardo Venier's Istrian possessions names the buyers as Nicolò and Marc'Antonio de Franceschi, sons of Giorgio. That join is on paper.

strands.label: Zorzi is Giorgio
strands.gen: the one inference this tree rests on
strands.note: Zorzi is simply the Venetian form of Giorgio. A document of 1730 directs that Zorzi's War of Candia pension be drawn at Capodistria — «probabilmente perchè la famiglia viveva già a Seghetto», because the family was already living at Seget. And Marc'Antonio was born in 1671, two years after Candia fell: a child of the flight, not of the island. Three separate grounds, no single record. Read as inferred.

strands.label: Nicolò, castellan of Milopotamo, about 1500
strands.note: The family's own account puts a castellan on Crete around 1500. Between him and Zorzi there is nothing at all. Same island, no join shown.

spines.name: Out of Corsica, to the Caribbean
spines.sub: Six generations · Ersa to Carabobo · 1694 to 1918
spines.lede: The one other complete descent this archive holds — and it is not this family. It is drawn here because a namesake line written from the inside, generation by generation, is the clearest possible demonstration of what «De Franceschi» is: a patronymic that grew wherever Italian was spoken, and grew twice without the two ever touching.

strands.label: Written from inside the family
strands.note: «LOS FRANCESCHI, la pequeña historia de una familia», Napoleón Franceschi González, Caracas 2002 — a historian's account of his own line, with dates to the day.

strands.label: Not one line touches Istria
strands.note: Six generations, twelve in-marrying Corsican families, and no contact of any kind with Istria, Carnia or Dalmatia. This is what an independent origin of the same surname looks like when somebody bothers to write it down.

strands.label: Tomino, one headland along
strands.note: The two Corsicans this archive actually holds — Cattarina, and Marie Jerome born Bastiani — are of Tomino, not Ersa, and no record has been read for either. Whether they belong to this line is unknown.
